name: CookieAz – Ley 21.719 Cookie Consent para Chile
author: cookieaz

sections.description:
CookieAz is the WordPress plugin built specifically for Chile’s Ley 21.719 on the protection of personal data.

It’s not a generic plugin translated from another regulation: it was built from the ground up around the terminology, deadlines, and rights that Chilean law requires, without concepts that don’t apply in this country. Many businesses already need to comply due to contractual requirements from clients or partners (banks, retail, public tenders), regardless of the law’s full enforcement date.

Key features

  • Cookie consent banner, with two color templates to choose from
  • Compatible with Google Consent Mode v2 (optional activation): your Google Ads campaigns and Analytics reports keep working correctly even when a visitor doesn’t accept cookies
  • Automatic blocking of third-party scripts (Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube videos, live chats) until the visitor accepts
  • Guided 8-step legal Wizard that generates your Cookie Policy and your Personal Data Processing Policy
  • Automatic creation of the legal pages on your site, or insertion via shortcode if you already have your own text
  • Consent log with a chained SHA-256 hash chain, exportable to CSV

Why choose CookieAz

Made in Chile, for Chile
Other well-known plugins were built for the European GDPR and later adapted to other laws. CookieAz was built directly around Ley 21.719.

Guided legal Wizard
You don’t need to copy legal text from the internet or know how to write a privacy policy. The Wizard walks you through it step by step using your company’s details and generates the documents for you.

Your campaigns and analytics keep working
CookieAz is compatible with Google Consent Mode v2, so even when a visitor doesn’t accept cookies, Google Ads and Google Analytics keep receiving aggregated signals and your reports aren’t left blind.

Verifiable consent log
Every consent is chained with a SHA-256 hash, so it can’t be altered afterward. If you ever need to prove compliance, the evidence is right there, and it’s yours: you can export it at any time.

Free, no monthly subscription
Many compliance solutions charge a recurring monthly fee, even just for the banner. CookieAz is free, with no limit on visits or subdomains.

What’s included in the free version

Everything described above is included at no cost. We’re preparing a Pro version with more complete evidentiary reports, a data-subject request (ARCOP) management panel, full banner customization, and multi-site licenses. If you’re interested, you can leave your email at cookieaz.cl to be notified when it’s available.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services:

  1. ipify.org — used to detect your own server’s public IP address, as the first step in detecting the hosting country for the international transfers section of the generated Data Processing Policy. It only runs when the site administrator clicks the “Auto-detect” button in step 1 of the legal Wizard — never on page load, never in the background, never on a schedule. No personal or visitor data is sent: only a request from the server itself asking for its own public IP.
    Service: https://www.ipify.org — Privacy policy: https://www.ipify.org/ (see site footer).

  2. ipapi.co — used to geolocate the public IP obtained from ipify.org, in order to suggest the hosting country. It runs immediately after the ipify.org request described above, as part of the same button click — it is not opt-in via a separate setting, but it never fires without that explicit administrator action. Only the server’s own public IP is sent, no visitor or personal data.
    Service: https://ipapi.co — Privacy policy: https://ipapi.co/privacy/.

  3. Supabase (CookieAz’s own backend) — optional, anonymous usage-data ping. It only runs if you explicitly enable the “Share anonymous usage data with CookieAz” option in Settings (disabled by default). Once a week (and immediately after enabling it), your site URL, plugin/WordPress/PHP version, and whether you used the legal Wizard are sent, so the plugin author can see which sites have CookieAz installed. No visitor data or legal/company configuration is ever sent.
    Service: https://supabase.com — Privacy policy: https://supabase.com/privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins > Add New in your WordPress admin panel
  2. Search for “CookieAz” and install the plugin
  3. Activate the plugin
  4. Go to the new CookieAz tab in your admin panel and follow the legal Wizard (8 steps): company details, legal pages, security, data origin, decisions, legitimate interest, services, and summary
  5. Choose whether you want CookieAz to automatically create the Cookie Policy and Data Processing Policy pages, use pages you already have, or insert them via shortcode
  6. Save, and you’re done — the banner is now active on your site
sections.faq:
Is a cookie banner mandatory in Chile?

Yes. If your site uses cookies that aren’t strictly necessary for it to function (analytics, advertising, social media), you need to inform visitors and ask for their consent before activating them. This is one of the core obligations of Ley 21.719.

I already have a cookie banner, do I still need CookieAz?

Possibly. Ley 21.719 requires non-essential cookies to stay blocked until the visitor decides, not just a notice while cookies keep firing anyway. Check whether your current banner actually blocks scripts before consent, or only displays a message — CookieAz implements that real blocking.

Is CookieAz compatible with Google Consent Mode v2?

Yes, optionally. If you enable it, consent signals are sent correctly to Google Analytics and Google Ads, without you having to configure anything yourself in Google’s tools.

Do I need to know about law or coding to use it?

No. The legal Wizard asks you simple questions about your company (name, tax ID, what data you process) and generates the documents and the banner for you.

What happens to Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, or other scripts I already have installed?

CookieAz detects them and blocks them until the visitor gives consent, without you having to touch your site’s code.

When does Ley 21.719 come into force?

The law has been in an adjustment period since its publication, with full enforcement set for December 1, 2026. Regardless of that date, many businesses already need to comply due to contractual requirements from clients or partners (banks, retail, public tenders).

What happens if my site doesn’t comply with Ley 21.719?

Sanctions range from warnings for minor infractions to fines of up to 20,000 UTM (Chilean tax units) in the most serious cases, plus being listed in the National Registry of Sanctions and Compliance for 5 years.

Is CookieAz useful if my site isn’t in Chile?

CookieAz is built specifically for Chile’s Ley 21.719. If your site operates under a different legal framework, you may need a different plugin or additional configuration.

Is it compatible with my WordPress theme?

Yes, CookieAz works independently of whatever theme you use.

How much does it cost?

The current version is completely free, with no limit on visits or subdomains. We’ll later launch an optional Pro version with additional features for businesses that need more control.

Can I use my own legal text instead of having CookieAz generate it?

Yes. In step 2 of the legal Wizard (Legal pages) you can choose between creating the page automatically, using a page you already have, or inserting the content via shortcode.

1.0.3

  • Corrección de empaquetado: se excluyen assets de marca no usados en tiempo de ejecución (íconos, favicons, lockups) para reducir el tamaño del plugin.

  • Restyling Azul Los Andes y negro, con compatibilidad para los esquemas guardados.
  • Sellos oficiales, icono de preferencias y crédito de marca by MacLucan actualizados.

  • First public release of CookieAz: cookie banner with real script blocking (includes optional Google Consent Mode v2 compatibility), 8-step legal Wizard to generate your legal pages, consent log with SHA-256 hash chain, exportable to CSV.
